source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client's telemetry shows ventricular tachycardia. At the bedside, what should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Checking responsiveness comes first. It shows whether the drop in cardiac output from VT is affecting the client. If unresponsive and pulseless, CPR begins.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q51 (PDF p. 191)
questions.quote: Determining unresponsiveness is the first assessment action to take.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client has late-stage salicylate poisoning with metabolic acidosis. Which serum value reflects acid-base balance?
questions.rationale: In acidosis, hydrogen ions move into cells and potassium moves out, causing hyperkalemia. Potassium therefore reflects the acid-base state.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q74 (PDF p. 219)
questions.quote: Hyperkalemia develops as the body attempts to compensate for the influx of H+ by moving H+ into the cell and potassium out of the cell

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child with lead poisoning is to receive chelation therapy. Which drug should the nurse prepare?
questions.rationale: EDTA is a chelating agent for lead poisoning. Activated charcoal reduces absorption in some poisonings, and sodium bicarbonate may be used for salicylate poisoning.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q120 (PDF p. 270)
questions.quote: EDTA is a chelating agent that is used to treat lead poisoning.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An IV nitroglycerin drip is started for an acute MI without an arterial line. Which bedside equipment ensures safety?
questions.rationale: Nitroglycerin dilates vessels, and its main side effect is hypotension. Without an arterial line, a noninvasive blood pressure monitor is used at the bedside.
explanations: Not specific to the drug's effect.
Not specific to the drug's effect.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q135 (PDF p. 285)
questions.quote: In the absence of an arterial monitoring line, the nurse should have a noninvasive blood pressure monitor for use at the bedside.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Concentrated IV lidocaine is ordered for ventricular tachycardia. Which solution should the nurse use to dilute it?
questions.rationale: The concentrated formulation of lidocaine must be diluted with 5% dextrose in water. Resuscitation equipment is kept available.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q145 (PDF p. 295)
questions.quote: The concentrated formulation must be diluted with 5% dextrose in water.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client suddenly has chest pain and dyspnea from a pulmonary embolus. How should the nurse position the client?
questions.rationale: Care includes semi-Fowler's position, oxygen, and IV analgesia (usually morphine). High Fowler's is avoided because extreme hip flexion slows venous return and promotes new clots.
explanations: Correct: eases breathing without hip flexion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q149 (PDF p. 299)
questions.quote: Fowler’s is avoided because extreme hip flexure slows venous return from the legs and increases the risk of new thrombi.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: PEEP of 7 cm is added to a client's ventilator. Which expected adverse effect should the nurse watch for?
questions.rationale: PEEP raises intrathoracic pressure and reduces cardiac output, shown by a lower systolic BP and a compensatory rise in pulse.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q220 (PDF p. 375)
questions.quote: PEEP leads to increased intrathoracic pressure, which in turn leads to decreased cardiac output.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding shows a LEFT tension pneumothorax is rapidly worsening?
options: Louder breath sounds on the left
questions.rationale: Tension pneumothorax causes tracheal deviation to the unaffected side, distended neck veins, decreased breath sounds on the affected side, worsening cyanosis, and falling BP.
explanations: Correct: shift away from the affected side.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q224 (PDF p. 379)
questions.quote: A tension pneumothorax is characterized by distended neck veins, displaced point of maximal impulse (PMI), tracheal deviation to the unaffected side

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with flail chest has PaO2 falling from 82 to 68 and PaCO2 rising from 44 to 51 in 2 hours. Which item should be at hand?
questions.rationale: Worsening respiratory acidosis in flail chest shows that the work of breathing is failing. Intubation and mechanical ventilation may be needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q238 (PDF p. 393)
questions.quote: The laboratory results indicate worsening respiratory acidosis.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Before giving an opioid through an epidural catheter, the nurse aspirates 5 mL of clear fluid. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Less than 1 mL of clear fluid fits epidural placement. More than 1 mL, or blood, means the catheter may be in the subarachnoid space or a vessel, so the drug is not given.
explanations: Correct: the catheter may be misplaced.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q240 (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: More than 1 mL of clear fluid or bloody return means that the catheter may be in the subarachnoid space or a vessel.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Mang Berto, 55, is rescued from a burning house and brought to the emergency room with respiratory distress.
questions.stem: Which test BEST shows whether Mang Berto has carbon monoxide poisoning?
questions.rationale: Serum carboxyhemoglobin directly measures CO poisoning. CO binds hemoglobin about 200 times more readily than oxygen, so pulse oximetry can be falsely normal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q264 (PDF p. 421)
questions.quote: Serum carboxyhemoglobin levels are the most direct measure of carbon monoxide poisoning

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Mang Berto, 55, is rescued from a burning house and brought to the emergency room with respiratory distress.
questions.stem: Mang Berto asks to remove his oxygen mask. Below which carboxyhemoglobin level can oxygen be safely removed?
questions.rationale: Oxygen may be removed once carboxyhemoglobin is below 5%. Levels of 10% to 20% cause headache, nausea, and dyspnea.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q246 (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Oxygen may be removed safely from the client with carbon monoxide poisoning once carboxyhemoglobin levels are less than 5%.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client arrives with upper GI bleeding that began 3 hours ago. What is the PRIORITY action?
questions.rationale: Vital signs show whether the client is in shock from blood loss and give a baseline to track treatment. Subjective data can wait until physical needs are met.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q254 (PDF p. 411)
questions.quote: The priority action for the client with GI bleeding is to obtain vital signs to determine whether the client is in shock from blood loss

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which intervention is standard when admitting a client with MI to the coronary care unit?
questions.rationale: Continuous cardiac monitoring is standard on CCU admission. Thrombolytics may or may not be prescribed and work best within the first 6 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q279 (PDF p. 436)
questions.quote: Standard interventions upon admittance to the CCU as they relate to this question include continuous cardiac monitoring.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with a thoracic spinal cord injury develops spinal shock. Which IV fluid does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Isotonic normal saline stays in the vascular space and raises intravascular volume and BP. Dextran is rarely needed and has adverse effects.
explanations: Does not stay in the vascular space.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q283 (PDF p. 441)
questions.quote: Normal saline 0.9% is an isotonic solution that primarily remains in the intravascular space, increasing intravascular volume.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which assessment BEST shows recovery from spinal shock?
questions.rationale: Spinal shock is marked by areflexia, so the return of reflexes shows recovery. Vital signs vary with many factors.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q307 (PDF p. 471)
questions.quote: Areflexia characterizes spinal shock; therefore, reflexes would provide the best information about recovery.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding is an EARLY sign that a cerebral aneurysm has ruptured?
questions.rationale: Rupture raises intracranial pressure, and the first sign is a change in level of consciousness, even subtle drowsiness or restlessness. Vital sign changes come later.
explanations: Correct: the earliest sign of rising ICP.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q308 (PDF p. 472)
questions.quote: The first sign of pressure in the brain is a change in the level of consciousness.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A home care nurse finds a client with a history of sertraline misuse unconscious. What should the nurse assess IMMEDIATELY?
questions.rationale: In an emergency, the nurse checks for breathing first, then pulse. Blood pressure and urine output come later.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q311 (PDF p. 475)
questions.quote: In an emergency situation, the nurse should determine breathlessness first and then assess for a pulse.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A unit of blood from the blood bank has gas bubbles in the bag. What should the nurse do?
options: Return it to the blood bank
questions.rationale: Gas bubbles suggest contamination, so the unit is returned. Nothing is ever added to blood, and filter tubing is always used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q312 (PDF p. 476)
questions.quote: the gas bubbles in the bag indicate possible contamination.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the SMALLEST IV catheter gauge acceptable for a blood transfusion?
questions.rationale: A 20-gauge or larger catheter prevents hemolysis of red cells and allows blood to flow without occluding the catheter.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q313 (PDF p. 477)
questions.quote: An intravenous catheter used to infuse blood should be at least 20 gauge or larger

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Thirty minutes into a packed RBC transfusion, the client reports itching and chest tightness. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: These are signs of a transfusion reaction. The nurse stops the transfusion first, then runs normal saline through new tubing, notifies the provider, and checks vital signs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q314 (PDF p. 478)
questions.quote: The first action of the nurse when a transfusion reaction is observed is to discontinue the transfusion.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which intervention belongs in the care plan for a client with a dissecting abdominal aortic aneurysm?
options: Teach that abdominal pain is expected
Encourage heavy lifting to regain strength
questions.rationale: The concern is rupture. The nurse checks peripheral circulation, watches for abdominal distention and lower-back ecchymoses, and has the client report abdominal pain.
explanations: Raises the pressure on the aneurysm.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q323 (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: The nurse should assess peripheral circulation and monitor for abdominal distention.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client is bleeding freely from a scalp laceration after a fall. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask about the last tetanus shot
questions.rationale: The first action is to stop the bleeding with direct pressure. The wound is then cleaned, assessed for suturing, and the tetanus status checked.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q330 (PDF p. 496)
questions.quote: The initial nursing action is to stop the bleeding, and direct pressure is applied.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Rodel, 22, is brought to the emergency room after a motorcycle crash with a possible closed head injury.
questions.stem: Which assessment should the nurse perform FIRST?
questions.rationale: The nurse first ensures an adequate airway and breathing, then circulation, then neurologic status.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q332 (PDF p. 498)
questions.quote: The first action of the nurse is to ensure that the client has an adequate airway and respiratory status.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.situation: Rodel, 22, is brought to the emergency room after a motorcycle crash with a possible closed head injury.
questions.stem: Six hours later, Rodel begins vomiting and reports dizziness and headache. What is the MOST important action?
options: Let him rest in the dark
questions.rationale: Headache, dizziness, and vomiting after a head injury suggest rising intracranial pressure, so the provider is notified at once.
explanations: Masks a sign of rising ICP.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q331 (PDF p. 497)
questions.quote: Increased ICP is evidenced by signs and symptoms such as headache, dizziness, confusion, weakness, and vomiting.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client is admitted after an overdose of an antipsychotic. What information is MOST important to obtain first?
options: Where and when it was taken
questions.rationale: In an emergency, lifesaving facts come first. The name and amount of drug taken guide treatment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q343 (PDF p. 511)
questions.quote: The name of and the amount of medication ingested is of utmost importance in treating this potentially life-threatening situation.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is the MOST common complication after myocardial infarction?
questions.rationale: Dysrhythmias are the most common complication and cause of death after MI. The others occur less often.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q355 (PDF p. 523)
questions.quote: Dysrhythmias are the most common complication and cause of death after an MI.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which finding at an IV site suggests infiltration?
options: Warm, red skin along the vein
questions.rationale: Infiltration is IV fluid leaking into tissue. It slows the rate and causes tenderness, swelling, skin tightness, and cool, blanched skin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q357 (PDF p. 525)
questions.quote: Infiltration is the leakage of an IV solution into the extravascular tissue.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client has acute cardiac and cerebral symptoms from fluid volume excess. Which measure increases comfort until therapy is ordered?
options: Raise the head of the bed to 45°
questions.rationale: Raising the head of the bed to 45 degrees reduces venous return to the heart and improves venous drainage from the brain. Oxygen needs a prescription.
explanations: Correct: reduces cardiac and cerebral load.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q360 (PDF p. 528)
questions.quote: Elevating the head of the bed to 45 degrees decreases venous return to the heart from the lower body

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: After CABG, mediastinal chest tube drainage drops from 75 mL in hour 1 to 5 mL in hour 2. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: About 500 mL is expected in the first 24 hours, up to 100 to 150 mL per hour early on. A sudden drop suggests the tube may be occluded, which can cause cardiac tamponade.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q396 (PDF p. 566)
questions.quote: The sudden drop in drainage between the first and second hour indicates that the tube is possibly occluded

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with silicosis has impending respiratory failure. Which equipment should be at the bedside?
questions.rationale: When compensatory mechanisms fail in respiratory failure, intubation and mechanical ventilation may be needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q434 (PDF p. 612)
questions.quote: The client with impending respiratory failure may need intubation and mechanical ventilation.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A continuous IV regular insulin infusion is ordered for a blood glucose of 700 mg/dL. How should it be given safely?
options: Run it on an infusion pump
Give it as an IV bolus
questions.rationale: An infusion pump prevents accidental overdose and hypoglycemia. Dextrose is added only once glucose falls to about 250 mg/dL.
explanations: Counteracts the treatment at this level.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q443 (PDF p. 623)
questions.quote: Insulin is administered via an infusion pump to prevent inadvertent overdose and subsequent hypoglycemia.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Synchronized cardioversion is planned for atrial fibrillation. Which action prevents a dangerous complication?
questions.rationale: In cardioversion, the shock is synchronized with the QRS complex so it does not fall during repolarization (the T wave), which could trigger ventricular fibrillation. Less energy is used than in defibrillation.
explanations: Less energy is used than in defibrillation.
Correct: synchronize with the QRS complex.
A shock on the T wave can cause VF.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q470 (PDF p. 654)
questions.quote: the countershock is synchronized to occur during ventricular depolarization (QRS complex)
